All records provisional.

characters.continuity: J.R.R. Tolkien Legendarium (The Lord of the Rings, The Silmarillion)
characters.summary: Landroval is a giant Eagle of the Misty Mountains, fighting primarily with aerial dives, talons, and beak strikes. He possesses immense natural flight capabilities and great physical strength.

mechanisms: Thick plumage and robust avian constitution

weaknesses: Vulnerable to ranged weaponry such as bows and arrows when exposed in flight
limitations: Physical stamina limits continuous high-load carriage over massive continental distances.

sources.supports: Landroval as a notable giant Eagle of the Misty Mountains who aids in battles.
Participation in historical battles including the rescue of Frodo and Sam from Mordor.

feats.claim: Flew to Mount Doom alongside Gwaihir and Meneldor to rescue Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Field of Cormallen

notableResults.note: Aided by Gwaihir and Meneldor in driving off the Nazgûl during the eruption of Mount Doom.

campaignTags.claim: Landroval is a giant Eagle possessing wings and native flight.
Landroval is described as a giant eagle capable of carrying heavy burdens.

unknowns: Exact wingspan and maximum lifting capacity beyond carrying two adult hobbits and gear are not precisely quantified.

characters.continuity: J.R.R. Tolkien Legendarium (The Lord of the Rings)
characters.summary: Legolas is a Sindar elf prince of Mirkwood who fights primarily as a master archer and skilled dual-blade swordsman. He relies on exceptional elf agility, keen senses, and swift ranged attacks.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to overwhelming numbers of heavy melee combatants if cornered in close quarters
mobility: Superhuman running speed over snow and terrain
limitations: Limited quiver capacity requiring careful arrow conservation during prolonged sieges.

sources.supports: Legolas's role as an elf of Mirkwood, master archer, and member of the Fellowship.
Feats of combat, weapons used, and notable engagements throughout the War of the Ring.

feats.claim: Shot down a Nazgûl's mount with a single arrow shot from a great distance at night.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Great River

feats.claim: Slain a Mumakil (Olog-hai/Oliphant) single-handedly by climbing it and shooting its eye.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Battle of the Pelennor Fields

notableResults.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Bridge of Khazad-dûm
notableResults.note: Standard skirmish engagement during the escape from Moria.

unknowns: Exact limits of elf endurance over multi-day forced marches without rest.

characters.summary: Lúthien is an Elf-maid of royal birth whose power is rooted in potent magic, song, and sleep-inducing enchantments. She avoids direct physical combat, instead neutralizing foes through powerful spells and illusions.
weaknesses: Physically vulnerable without her magical preparations or protective spells
limitations: Spellcasting requires concentration and vocal/musical execution.

sources.supports: Lúthien's lineage as daughter of Thingol and Melian, and her magical powers.
Feats including putting Morgoth to sleep and entering Angband.

feats.claim: Put Morgoth and his entire court into a deep magical sleep using her song and spellcraft.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

feats.claim: Enchanted and dismantled Sauron's fortress of Tol-in-Gaurhoth.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

notableResults.note: Successfully put the Dark Lord to sleep to steal a Silmaril from his iron crown.

campaignTags.claim: Lúthien wields potent elven and Maia-derived magic through song and glamour.
Cast spells of profound sleep and illusion that affected even Dark Lords.

unknowns: The absolute limits of her song against beings entirely devoid of hearing or mind.

characters.summary: Mablung of the Heavy Hand is a renowned Elven captain of Doriath, fighting as an expert swordsman and tracker. He is stalwart in defense and experienced in forest warfare.
weaknesses: Mortally susceptible to overwhelming force or betrayal by allies
limitations: Human-level physical attributes compared to Maia or high-tier lords.

sources.supports: Mablung's role as chief captain of Thingol and defender of Doriath.

feats.claim: Led guards of Doriath in tracking and capturing the mischievous Orc bands and guarding the borders.

unknowns: Full record of individual combat victories outside general campaign mentions.

characters.summary: Maedhros the Tall is an Eldar prince of the House of Fëanor, renowned as a peerless warrior and commander. He fights with sword and spear, famously continuing to fight fiercely even after losing his right hand.
weaknesses: Psychological torment stemming from the Oath of Fëanor and previous torture
limitations: Missing his right hand, relying solely on left-handed or modified grips.

sources.supports: Maedhros's status as eldest son of Fëanor, his rescue from Thangorodrim, and military leadership.
Combat feats, leadership in the Wars of Beleriand, and ambidextrous fighting style.

feats.claim: Survived hanging by the wrist from Thangorodrim for years before amputation of his right hand, later learning to fight effectively with his left hand.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Flight of the Noldor

feats.claim: Commanded the Union of Maedhros in the massive Battle of Unnumbered Tears (Nirnaeth Arnoediad).
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Nirnaeth Arnoediad

notableResults.note: Defeated due to betrayal by Easterlings during the battle.

unknowns: Precise tally of individual duels against major Orc commanders.

characters.summary: Maglor is a Noldorin prince, poet, singer, and warrior, son of Fëanor. He fights with sword and bow, combining martial prowess with legendary musical and vocal skill.
weaknesses: Tormented by remorse over the Oath of Fëanor
limitations: Bound by the cursed Oath of Fëanor, driving self-destructive actions.

sources.supports: Participation in the Kinslayings and Wars of Beleriand.

feats.claim: Defended the Gap of Maglor and fought in all major battles of the First Age of Beleriand.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Return of the Noldor

notableResults.opponent: Defenders of the Havens of Sirion
notableResults.note: Kinslaying engagement to recover a Silmaril.

unknowns: Exact fate after casting himself into the sea with a Silmaril.
Unverified (cited source failed the automatic check): Fostered Elros and Elrond after the sack of the Havens of Sirion.

characters.summary: Melian is a Maia of Valinor and Queen of Doriath, wielding immense divine and magical power. She creates impenetrable protective barriers (the girdle of Melian) and possesses supreme foresight and mind-speech.
weaknesses: Gained physical form and vulnerability through love for Thingol, leading to grief and sorrow upon his death.
mobility: Flight or spiritual transport in Valinor, standard physical movement in Middle-earth
limitations: Bound within physical form in Middle-earth, restricting direct divine intervention.

sources.supports: Melian's nature as a Maia, Queen of Doriath, and creator of the Girdle of Melian.
Powers of enchantment, telepathy, and defensive warding of the forest.

feats.claim: Created the Girdle of Melian, an impenetrable labyrinth of shadow and bewilderment that protected the entire realm of Doriath for millennia.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Thingol and Melian

feats.claim: Perceived the approach of evil and communicated warnings telepathically across Beleriand.

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Darkening of Valinor
notableResults.note: Combined efforts with Oromë drove away Ungoliant, though Melian's wards later contained her entry into Doriath.

campaignTags.claim: Melian is a Maia possessing divine magical and spiritual power.
Wove the magical Girdle of Melian around Doriath.
Communicated over vast distances using thought and mind-speech.

unknowns: Full extent of her combat capabilities if forced into direct physical offense.

characters.continuity: J.R.R. Tolkien Legendarium (The Lord of the Rings)
characters.summary: Meriadoc 'Merry' Brandybuck is a Hobbit of the Shire who rises to become a warrior of Rohan and knight of Gondor. He fights with a short sword, barrow-blade, and dagger, relying on stealth, courage, and specialized anti-magic weaponry.
weaknesses: Standard hobbit physical strength and fragility against direct heavy attacks
limitations: Hobbit stature limits reach and raw striking power against large opponents.

sources.supports: Merry's background as hobbit of the Shire, squire of Rohan, and participant in the War of the Ring.
Use of the barrow-blade to stab the Witch-king of Angmar.

feats.claim: Stabbed the Witch-king of Angmar behind the knee with an ancient westernesse blade, breaking the spell protecting the wraith from mortal harm.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Battle of the Pelennor Fields

notableResults.note: Assisted Éowyn by striking the Witch-king's hamstring from behind, enabling his destruction.

conditional.ability: Piercing the invulnerability of the Witch-king
conditional.dependsOn: Using a Barrow-blade enchanted specifically against Angmar

campaignTags.claim: Wields a barrow-blade forged by Westernesse with anti-magic properties against wraiths.

unknowns: Combat effectiveness against standard armored human soldiers without surprise.

characters.summary: Morgoth, formerly Melkor, is the supreme Dark Lord and a fallen Vala. He fights with colossal physical strength, a massive war-hammer called Grond, elemental fire, and overwhelming dark sorcery, though he has diminished his native power by pouring it into the matter of Arda.
weaknesses: Permanently bound to physical form, capable of feeling pain, fatigue, and permanent scarring from wounds.
limitations: Significantly diminished in personal combat agility and total energy compared to his original stature due to dispersing his power into Arda.

sources.supports: Morgoth's status as the chief antagonist, fallen Vala, and master of Angband.
Use of Grond, combat with Fingolfin, and elemental powers.

feats.claim: Fought Fingolfin in single combat, ultimately crushing him after sustaining several severe sword wounds.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Beleriand

feats.claim: Created dragons, balrogs, and hordes of Orcs through corruption and dark power.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Coming of the Elves

notableResults.note: Won the duel, but received permanent foot and facial scars from Fingolfin's sword Ringil.
Face scarred by the giant eagle Thorondor when Thorondor rescued Fingolfin's body.

campaignTags.claim: Morgoth wields supreme dark divine magic as a fallen Vala.
Casts curses and binds wills through dark sorcery.
Emits elemental fire and breath of dragons.

unknowns: The exact upper limit of his power output at his peak prior to creating Arda Marred.

characters.continuity: J.R.R. Tolkien Legendarium (The Silmarillion / History of Middle-earth)
characters.summary: Melkor Unbound represents Melkor at a primordial, cosmic scale before he scattered his native power into the physical matter of Arda. He fights with unimaginable divine might, elemental cataclysms, and absolute cosmic supremacy.
weaknesses: Pride and discord leading to eventual rebuff by united Valar
mobility: Cosmic flight and divine teleportation across stellar/universal realms
limitations: Subject to the collective ruling authority of Eru Ilúvatar and the combined Valar.
characters.formDifferences: This form represents Melkor at his absolute primordial peak before dispersing his divine essence into the physical fabric of Middle-earth (Arda), granting him vastly greater energy, scale, and invulnerability than his later 'Morgoth' persona.

sources.supports: Melkor's original status as the most powerful Ainur created by Eru Ilúvatar.
Description of his unminished state during the shaping of Arda before his power was poured into the earth.

notableResults.note: Subdued and bound by Tulkas and the host of Valar during the early shaping of Arda.

campaignTags.claim: Melkor wields supreme primordial divine power as the most powerful of the Ainur.
Manipulates reality and elemental forces on a cosmic scale.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of his pre-Arda combat engagements against individual Valar prior to recorded history.
